title: 3. Exposition: Foundations
use_cases: Use when establishing the backdrop of a story to immerse readers.
Implement when introducing protagonists and antagonists to set conflict.
Configure when defining time, place, and atmosphere to anchor the narrative.
Use when designing a key event that disrupts normalcy and initiates the plot.
Apply when outlining the narrative arc to guide story development.
content:
Setting the stage is vital—think of it as laying the groundwork for a house before you build the rooms.

- Setting: Time, place, atmosphere. Example: In The Great Gatsby, the opulent 1920s New York skyline sets up the era’s decadence.
- Characters: Protagonist(s), antagonist(s), supporting roles. Example: Harry Potter’s introduction as a boy living with his abusive aunt establishes his vulnerability.
- Inciting Incident: Event that disrupts normalcy and starts the plot. Example: In The Hunger Games, Katniss volunteering for her sister triggers the entire narrative.
